author: Subhadip Kanjilal
why: Photographer explicitly identifies this as a wild gaur in Jaldapara National Park, India, despite the generic page title. Standing forest-path candidate; sex, native dimensions and exact crop unverified.

author: Saketh Upadhya
why: Photographer identifies the grazing animal as gaur in Ooty, Tamil Nadu, rather than domestic cattle. Green habitat alternative; mature-bull status, native dimensions and full-body crop unverified.

author: Petra Ryan
why: Caption identifies wild gaur grazing in India; source lists 6720×4480 and Canon EOS 5D Mark IV capture. High-resolution option, but full-body framing, sex and watermark status unverified.

author: akhil
why: Source identifies gaur/Bos gaurus at Ooty, India, and lists 6000×4000 with Nikon D3500 capture. Lush setting and ample resolution; close-up fallback with sex and full-body visibility unverified.

author: Prema Ganapathy
why: Caption explicitly confirms Bos gaurus in the Nilgiris. Free-ranging animal in a garden/tea-estate context, a habitat compromise. Dimensions, full-body framing and watermark status unverified.

author: Sundaresh Ramanathan
why: Caption explicitly confirms Bos gaurus at Bandipur National Park. Species and Indian location established; 1024px fallback. Noncommercial/no-derivatives licence; framing and watermark status unverified.

author: Ajeesh VS
why: Photo caption explicitly identifies Indian Gaur, Bos gaurus. Forest-clearing composition with a substantial dark animal; supplied 1920-size rendition is below preference. Watermark status unverified.

author: Prashant S. Gupta
why: Photographer documents a dominant wild bull at Bandhavgarh, with dorsal ridge, curved horns and white lower legs. Strong subject match, though branches obscure parts of the animal; resolution unverified.

author: Steven Falk
why: Title explicitly identifies a resting gaur bull in the Western Ghats, Goa. Confirmed male fallback, but resting pose limits leg visibility; 1024px rendition and unverified watermark status.

author: Peter Connolly
why: Photographer identifies gaur in Bandipur National Park, Karnataka. Documented Indian wild-habitat candidate; 1024px fallback. Sex, full-body framing and watermark status unverified.

author: Syed Ahmad
why: Gaur article credits this forest photograph to Syed Ahmad/Unsplash. Muscular animal with pale stockings and prominent shoulder ridge; original dimensions, precise location and watermark status unverified.
